subject: Operational readiness alignment — reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@northbridge.com>; Elena Torres <elena.torres@northbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational readiness alignment — reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from Redwood and a proposed set of next steps so we're aligned before engineering digs in. I focused this note on availability and graceful degradation since that was your top concern.

Key pain points you described:
- Recent multi-region incident (2027-02-19): failover took ~18 minutes, customer-facing timeouts for peak batch jobs.
- Heavy burst traffic during end-of-month processing that overwhelms your pooled endpoints.
- Lack of automated fallback to smaller / quantized model variants when GPUs are constrained.

What success looks like (Northbridge criteria):
- 99.95% P99 token latency for interactive workflows during business hours.
- Clear, automatic downgrade path: regional fallback + model-variant fallback with no SLA-blind period.
- Post-incident runbook that reduces failover time to <5 minutes (target).

Current stack you shared:
- Frontend routing: internal LB -> API gateway -> k8s service fronting model pool.
- Models: mix of fine-tuned LLMs (24B/32B) hosted on a managed GPU cluster.
- Observability: custom Prometheus + internal alerts; no token-level cost tracing yet.

Immediate risks we flagged on the call:
1) Cold KV cache and no persistent prefix caching means higher token compute on replays.
2) No automatic downgrade policy in the orchestration layer.
3) Single-region ingress for critical endpoints.

Recommended next steps (proposal):
1) Pilot Redwood’s graceful-degradation setup in a staging namespace:
   - Configure model variant chain: full precision -> quantized 8-bit -> distilled 7B fallback.
   - Enable automatic region-based routing with passive health probing.
2) Run a synthetic failover exercise with our SREs (2 hours) to measure failover time and identify bottlenecks.
3) Share an SLA draft (attached) with P99 targets and an escalation matrix; we can iterate.

Proposed owners and timeline:
- Redwood (Priyom / Karthik): pilot config + runbook + 2-hour failover exercise (ETA 2 weeks).
- Northbridge (Samir / Elena): grant staging access and share the service map for the primary ingestion path (attached request).

Attachments: [Attachment: service_map_v1.pdf (PDF, 240KB)], [Attachment: NB-SLA-draft.docx (DOCX, 28KB)].

Are you good with the pilot scope? If yes I’ll send calendar invites and a read-only staging service role.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@northbridge.com>

Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@northbridge.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness alignment — reliability & graceful degradation

Priyom —

Appreciate the concise summary. That's an accurate capture of what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The incident on 2027-02-19 was compounded by an upstream gateway flapping; failover automation exists but isn’t hooked to model-variant policies. So even when the region is marked degraded, we still serve high-cost models until infra operators intervene.
- Our compliance team requires audit logs for any automated downgrade; can Redwood provide token/decision-level logs for the pilot?

We're okay to proceed with the pilot. For timing: the last week of April is ideal for our ops availability window.

Action items we can take before the pilot:
- Share the staging VPC peering request and a short service map (I’ll attach a sanitized diagram).
- Provide a list of endpoints that need the strictest P99 (we'll send this by Wed).

Also: can you confirm whether your graceful-deg approach supports region fallback first, then model downgrade? That order matters for our data locality constraints.

Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering — Northbridge Financial
samir.gupta@northbridge.com | +1 (617) 555-0199
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness alignment — reliability & graceful degradation

Thanks Samir / Priyom —

Short answers from the Redwood engineering side:
- Audit logging: yes, we can enable token-decision logs for the pilot with retention configurable per your compliance needs. We’ll provide a sample schema before the exercise.
- Fallback order: we can configure policy chains; default pattern is region fallback -> model-variant downgrade -> graceful response (if configured). We can flip that order if Northbridge prefers model-first.

Prep checklist I’ll own before the pilot:
- Build staging model chain manifest and share by 2027-04-11.
- Prepare a short runbook for the failover exercise (20–30 minutes read).
- Coordinate SRE slots for the actual exercise (need a 2-hour block).

I’ll start the manifest today and loop in Monica for the SLA wording.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Good to hear April week works. Next immediate items (I’ll action these today):

- Share the read-only staging IAM role + VPC peering template.

Cheers,
